title: After the rain
question: Why is part of Pine Creek muddier and quicker this morning?

intro.speaker: Ranger Wren
lines: Pine Creek isn't the same color the whole way. Walk it. Measure what you can. Don't decide from the station porch.

sites.name: Rain gauge
sites.observe: Last night's marks sit higher than the rest of the week. It rained. That doesn't say where the mud came from.

sites.name: Creek below the station
sites.observe: The water here still looks about as clear as a quiet morning.

sites.name: Where Fox Run meets Pine Creek
sites.observe: A brown thread joins the creek here. The water looks quicker than it did up by the station.

sites.name: Fresh scar on Westface
sites.observe: Loose soil, a bite out of the slope, and Fox Run starting right below it.

sites.name: Cattail marsh
sites.observe: The marsh is tea-colored, the way it often is. It isn't pulsing brown the way the creek is above the pond.

sites.name: Willow Reach
sites.observe: Mud still hangs in the water downstream. Some of it is already dropping out.

sites.name: High Look
sites.observe: From here the brown line starts where the little run meets Pine Creek, not at the pond.

sites.name: Instrument crate
sites.observe: A note about not leaving the meter in the marsh. Nothing about this morning's mud.

explanations.label: Rain loosened Westface soil. Fox Run carried it into Pine Creek.
It rained, so the whole creek is muddier.
explanations.hint: The stretch by the station is still relatively clear. Rain fell on more than one place.

explanations.label: Mirror Pond overflowed and sent mud downstream.
explanations.hint: The brown water shows up where Fox Run joins, above the pond.

followUp.prompt: The marsh is brownish most days. Does that change the story?

options.label: Then the marsh caused it.
options.hint: The pulse of mud is above the pond, where the tributary joins.

options.label: The marsh isn't the pulse I measured.

success: Rain, a loose slope, and a tributary did this together. That's a system, not a single culprit.
wrenAfter: You know how to work a problem now. High Country will ask you to work out where you are.
